chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from one of our companions, from Ibrahim ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Waddah, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Umm Khalid al-Abdiyyah came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I was in his presence. So she said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The growling in my stomach is squeezing me.' She asked him about the ailments of women and said, 'The physicians of Iraq have prescribed Al-Nabeez with Al-Suweq for me, and I paused because I recognized your dislike for it, so I wished to ask you about that.' He said to her, 'And what prevents you from drinking it?' She said, 'I have emulated you in my religion, so when I meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, whenever I meet Him, I can tell Him that Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) ordered me and forbade me.'

He said, 'O Abu Muhammad! Do you listen to this woman and this question? By Allah, I do not grant you permission for one drop of it, and do not taste from it one drop, for you will regret when your soul reaches here.' And he gestured with his hand to his throat, saying it to her three times: 'Did you understand?' She said, 'Yes.'
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What wets the needle, dirties a container of water,' saying it to her three times.

key_terms.السَّوِيق: Al-Suweq (a type of flour or grain meal, often used as a base or accompaniment)
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Al-Nabeez (a specific type of fermented drink, often from dates or grapes)
key_terms.حُبّاً: Hubban (a small amount/container, often referring to a vessel or a handful)
key_terms.قَرَاقِرُ: Qaraqir (growling or gurgling sound in the stomach)
key_terms.قَلَّدْتُكَ دِينِي: Qalladtu ka deeni (I have emulated/followed you in my religion)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on consuming fermented drinks for medical purposes according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Umm Khalid seeks the Imam’s ruling on consuming Al-Nabeez for medicinal purposes, highlighting the Shia principle of *takhassus* (specialization) where the layperson defers to the Imam’s judgment. The Imam’s emphatic prohibition, repeated three times, underscores the severity of wine even when used for cure, while his statement that it 'pollutes water' illustrates the concept of *kathir* (abundant) becoming impure through the addition of a small amount of *qalil* (scant) wine, a key juristic distinction. This narrative reinforces the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in resolving practical medical and ritual questions, bridging physical health with spiritual purity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from one of our companions, from Ibrahim Bin Khalid, from Abdullah Bin Wazza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Umm Khalid Al-Abdiyat came over to Abu Abdullahasws and I was in hisasws presence. So she said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! The growling in my stomach is squeezing me’, so she asked about the pains of the women and she said, ‘The physicians of Al-Iraq have prescribed Al-Nabeez with Al-Suweyq, but I paused for I do recognise yourasws dislike for it, therefore I would like to ask youasws about that’. So heasws said to her: ‘And what prevents you from drinking it?’ She said, ‘I have emulated youasws in my Religion (Taqleed), so when I meet Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, whenever I do meet Himazwj, so I can tell Himazwj that Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws had ordered me and forbade me’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! Did you listen to this lady and this question? No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I<sup>asws</sup> do not allow for you with regards to one drop from it, and do not taste from it one drop, for you would be regretful when your soul reaches over here’ – and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured by his<sup>asws</sup> hand to his<sup>asws</sup> throat, saying it to her three (times): ‘Did you understand?’ She said, ‘Yes’.
Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What dampens the needle, dirties a container of water’ – saying it to her three (times)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from certain persons of our people from Ibrahim ibn Khalid from ‘Abd Allah ibn Waddah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam when the mother of Khalid al-‘Abdiyah visited him (the Imam). She said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause. I have a growling condition in my belly [I asked a women with such condition about it and she said] the physicians of Iraq have prescribed for her al-Nabidh with sawiq; but I have learned and I know that you dislike it and I like to ask you about it. He (the Imam) asked, ‘What stops you from drinking it?’ She replied, ‘I have taken upon myself to follow your instructions in matters of my religion so upon my meeting with Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, I will be able to tell Him that Ja‘far ibn Muhammad commanded and prohibited me.’

He (the Imam) asked, ‘O abu Muhammad, do you hear this woman and these issues? No, by Allah, I will not give you permission, not even for one drop of it and you must not taste even one drop of it because you, otherwise, will regret when the soul reaches here’, pointing to his throat, ‘Did you understand?’ She replied, ‘Yes, I understand?

He (the Imam) then said, ‘A small amount of it (wine) that can hardly moisten an applicator of kohl (eyeliner) to the eye can make a whole hub (a large water container) filthy? He (the Imam) said it three times?”
